newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-MARK WAUGH HITS 124 AS AUSTRALIA EDGE AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MARK WAUGH HITS 124 AS AUSTRALIA EDGE AHEAD.

text.p: Mark Waugh stroked a confident 124 as Australia edged ahead of Natal by 35 runs on first innings on the second day of their four-day match against at Kingsmead on Friday.
Although Waugh was the only one of the Australian top six to establish himself significantly on another hot day, his side batted positively to extend their overnight 23 without loss to 370 all out.

Off-spinner Pat Symcox, who troubled all the batsmen, bowled with intelligent variation of flight and pace to take four for 117, and advance his claims for a place in the South African side for next Thursday's first test in Johannesburg.
At the close, Natal were 21 without loss in their second innings, still 14 runs behind.
Waugh survived a sharp stumping chance on eight and a scorching return catch to Symcox on 79 but otherwise moved relentlessly to his 61st first-class century off 136 balls.

With useful support from Matthew Elliott (38), brother Steve Waugh (22) and a fluent Michael Bevan (52), the New South Wales all-rounder orchestrated solid stands of 76, 71 and 74 as Australia maintained a run rate of four an over for most of their innings.

Waugh eventually departed after cutting the medium pace of Natal captain Dale Benkenstein head-high to cover, having been at the crease for just over three hours, faced 152 deliveries and struck 13 fours and four sixes.
Leg-spinner Shane Warne clubbed three sixes and five fours in a quick-fire 44 from 33 balls as the tourists moved into the lead.

Earlier, the left-handed Australian openers extended their partnership to 65 before captain Mark Taylor (20) tamely popped a return catch to Symcox, who struck again two overs later when Matthew Hayden (28) flicked the ball uppishly to Errol Stewart at mid-wicket.
